title: Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Huna
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a distinguished student of Abaye and Rava, as in Berakhot 34b, where he said, “I saw Abaye and Rava leaning sideways [in prayer]” (in Megillah 22a Hyman considers its bar Avin reading erroneous); likewise Yoma 53b, where he said, “I saw Abaye and Rava take three steps in a single bow”; and in Niddah 40a he spoke in Rava’s name. In Keritot 25a, “Rabbi Chiyya recited a baraita before Rava”; Hyman suggests that perhaps it should read “son of Rav Huna.” Likewise in Ketubot 35b, “Rav Chiyya said to Rava,” Hyman suggests that perhaps it should read Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna; and in Berakhot 34b, “Rav Chiyya said that Rav Safra said,” Hyman suggests that perhaps he is Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna. He is mentioned in Shabbat 5a, resolving Rabbi Zeira’s words: “for example, where he caught it from on top of the wall.”
In Pesachim 44b he said: “The Torah forbade only [flavor from] a pot used that day”; in Avodah Zarah 67b Hyman regards as corrupt the reading Rav Huna bar Chiyya.

In Yevamot 119b: “Rav Papa said … Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna said: when she says, ‘He and I hid in a cave.’” There, at 81b, he resolves [it] as dissolved. In Menachot 42b he sent in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: “On the hand-tefillin one says … ‘to put on tefillin,’” etc.; Dikdukei Soferim cites the reading Rav Acha bar Huna, and Hyman prefers this reading.

notes.text: The heading fully writes Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Huna; body Rav forms and the proposed bar Avin/Huna bar Chiyya/Acha alternatives remain distinct. The pot statement concerns its absorbed flavor rather than prohibiting the vessel as food. All identifications and preferred corrections remain Hyman’s, and taught-before-Rava is the reciter role.

Berakhot 34b directly names Chiyya son of Huna observing Abaye and Rava leaning. The other proposed bar Avin, Huna bar Chiyya and Acha substitutions remain occurrence-specific Hyman judgments; the exact Dikdukei Soferim reading was not inspected. The pot statement concerns absorbed flavor, and reciting before Rava is a role rather than a new tannaitic-era assignment.
